To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified seven cellular genes as co-factors for CD4 down-reguation and four of these genes are also involved in HIV replication.
we identified seven cellular co-factors of HIV-1-mediated early endocytic CD4 down-regulatory events and four of them also affect HIV-1 infection in T cells.
we identified 55 genes that are involved in HIV-1-mediated down-regulation of CD4 from the surface of cells and we validated 7 of these genes in a second cell line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new targets for the development of novel antivirals.
the identification of cellular co-factors involved in HIV-1-mediated down-modulation of CD4 and HIV-1 replication.
the identification and characterization of host factors involved in HIV-1-mediated down-regulation of the HIV receptor CD4 and their possible involvement in viral replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these genes are not involved in CD4 trafficking but in HIV-1 infection, but the exact role of these genes in HIV-1 pathogenesis still remains to be elucidated.

the genes identified here are not only involved in HIV-1-mediated down-modulation of the HIV-1 co-receptor CD4, but also affect other steps in HIV-1 replication, which needs to be addressed by further research.
the knock-down or inhibition of any of these proteins could be considered as a potential target to develop new anti-HIV-1 drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the knock-downs of EPS15, IDH3, ATP6AP1 and DNM3 can increase CD4 levels and decrease HIV-1 replication, which is in accordance with their function in HIV-1-mediated down-modulation of CD4.

the knock-downs of EPS15, Dnm3, ATP6AP1 and IDH3G have an inhibitory effect on HIV-1 infection, while the knock-downs on HRBL and HSP90B have no effect and the knock-down of SNX22 has a stimulatory effect on HIV- 1 infection.
the knock-downs of EPS15, Dnm3, ATP6AP1 and IDH3G significantly increases CD4 expression levels and decreases HIV-1 infection levels in T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of shRNA screening and validation in HIV-1 infected primary cells can identify cellular factors involved in HIV-1 infection.
the identification of cellular factors that affect HIV-1-induced down-regulation of the CD-4 receptor may lead to the development of new therapeutic targets for anti-HIV-1 drugs.
HIV-1 uses a complex machinery for the internalization of CD4 and the subsequent degradation of the CD4-receptor, which involves a number of host factors that are involved in endocytic processes.
